html:
SMTO-WEB-0016 — SMTO couldn't find the website you asked it to read

GUID: 87438285-20b9-4c67-a9e5-b881432c2ac3
Slug: web-dns-failed
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO looked up the website's name, but the network returned no address for it, so the page was not read. Nothing was downloaded or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the web address in your request for typos, such as a missing letter or a wrong ending like .con instead of .com, and correct it. A misspelled website name has no address, which is exactly what the lookup reported.
  2. On the computer running SMTO, open the same address in a web browser. If the browser also says the site can't be found, the problem is the name or that computer's network, not SMTO.
  3. If other websites also fail on that computer, ask the person who manages its network to check its internet and name-lookup (DNS) settings. SMTO uses that computer's own network settings to find websites.
  4. Once the address opens in a browser, ask SMTO to read the page again. Reading a public page changes nothing, so it is safe to repeat once the lookup works.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the page and shows its content or a summary instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the exact web address, to the person who manages SMTO or your network. Don't replace the website name with a numeric address to get around this; SMTO checks names to keep requests away from private networks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Web transport name resolution (socket.getaddrinfo in skills/web/transport.py _resolve) returned an empty address list for the requested host, so no connection was attempted.

What this means

  • DNS resolution returns an empty usable-address list for the requested hostname. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • DNS resolution returns an empty usable-address list for the requested hostname.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the hostname and resolver result from the execution host.

How to fix it

  • Resolve the same hostname on the SMTO Server host (for example with getent hosts or dig) and fix the hostname or the host's DNS resolver configuration; then repeat the read. Do not substitute an unchecked IP literal to bypass the public-address validation.
  • Check the hostname and resolver on the execution host. Retry the read after DNS is corrected; do not weaken private-address restrictions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • DNS provides an eligible address and ordinary public-target validation still passes.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass private-address validation by replacing the hostname with an unchecked IP address.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
